message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I did the right thing by saying "See you next year!" to my teacher who's getting let go. Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. The teacher, let's call him R, was new this year. He imposed his own teaching methods, which were very different from what we were used to. Even when people pointed out that his methods were wrong, he still expected us to follow them. He took off points for scratch work he didn't like and tried to deduct as many points as possible on tests, quizzes, and homework. Every student he had was subjected to this. He also took forever to grade our assignments. We took a test before spring break and got it back about six weeks later. He refused to go over it with anyone. Plus, he never offered help outside the classroom and was hostile when asked for extra help. The administration noticed all this, and we were told R isn't coming back next year. We were all really happy about that. Since the announcement, R completely checked out. He wrote notes on the board, barely talked during class, and even went to Disneyland instead of attending one of the review days for exams. Yesterday, as I was walking out of R's classroom for the last time, I called over my shoulder, "See you next year!" My friends told me I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. Is AITA (Ask If Terrible Advice)? Now, I need to think about whether my action was right or wrong. Let's consider the possible perspectives. From my perspective, R was a bad teacher. He was unfair, didn't help students, and was hostile. The administration agreed he wasn't coming back, so we were all relieved. Saying "See you next year!" might seem like I'm being sarcastic or mocking his situation. But I didn't mean it that way. I was just making a comment as I left, knowing he wasn't coming back. Maybe I was trying to be funny or just making an offhand remark. From R's perspective, he was already checked out. He wasn't engaging with us, went to Disneyland instead of reviewing, and was probably feeling down about being let go. My comment might have been hurtful or added to his stress. Even if I didn't mean it maliciously, it could have been perceived that way. From my friends' perspective, they think I was being an asshole. They might see it as mocking someone who's already in a tough spot. They might feel that it's not kind to make a comment like that, especially when someone is leaving and might be feeling bad about it. So, is it right or wrong? Well, it's a bit of a gray area. On one hand, I didn't mean any harm, and I was just making a comment. On the other hand, R was in a vulnerable position, and my comment could have been seen as insensitive or mocking. I should also consider the impact of my words. Even if I didn't mean it negatively, the way it was said or the context could make it seem like I was being sarcastic. R might have taken it the wrong way, especially since he was already upset about being let go. In terms of personal feelings, I was happy that R wasn't coming back because he was a bad teacher. But does that give me the right to make a comment that could be seen as mocking? Probably not. It's better to be kind, even to someone you don't like, especially when they're in a difficult situation. So, in conclusion, while I didn't mean any harm, the comment could have been perceived as insensitive or mocking. Therefore, it might not have been the best thing to say. My friends might be right in thinking that I was being an asshole, even if I didn't intend it that way.
